clue.text: Queries cap to be fixed for novel form

indicators.note: letters that are to be fixed are put right by being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer queries which hat a character should wear before settling on a style of novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The picaresque is a genre of fiction following the episodic adventures of a roguish hero, as in Don Quixote.

clue.text: Advance when yours truly leaves job

indicators.note: leaves means goes out of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to advance an idea is to posit it
yours truly is the speaker, I

explanation.surface: Someone gets promoted when the writer quits their employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a position of employment, a job.

clue.text: Unambiguous article on church will get authorization

parts.note: unambiguous means clear
an is the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A precise piece about a church will win official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is official permission or authorisation, as for take-off or for secret material.

clue.text: Sack head of finance in anger

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to rile someone is to anger them

indicators.note: the head is the first letter

explanation.surface: A finance director is fired in a fit of rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like dismiss but means plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search and rob it, to sack it.

clue.text: Scouse is different across river — that's sweet!

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so it goes round the other letter
being different means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: The Liverpool accent sounds different over the Mersey, and a delight.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouse is the Liverpool accent or dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucrose is common table sugar, a sweet substance.

clue.text: Positive aspects of winning teams

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead, winning
sides are teams

explanation.surface: Good points of the victorious sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsides are advantages, the positive aspects of a situation.

clue.text: Catch on — shoot!

definitions.meaning: to grasp or realise something, informal
a young slender branch of a plant

explanation.surface: Someone finally understands, and exclaims in triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal for to understand suddenly; a twig is also a small shoot growing from a branch.

clue.text: Walked off, missing kilometres in wooded area

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
missing means without the letter

parts.note: K is short for kilometres

explanation.surface: Someone strolled away without covering much distance in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops K from WALKED; 'off' rearranges WALED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weald is a once-forested region of south-east England; the word means wooded country.

clue.text: Dull affair that shows intelligence

parts.note: dull, overcast weather is grey
an affair is a matter or business

explanation.surface: A boring business that nonetheless displays brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey matter is the brain tissue, so informally brains or intelligence.

clue.text: With no source of sugar, amrita is a poor drink

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are rearranged
with no means the letter is removed
a source is a start, the first letter

explanation.surface: Unsweetened divine nectar makes a disappointing beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Amrita is the nectar of immortality in Hindu myth. 'With no' takes S from AMRITAISA; 'poor' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a coffee liqueur, a brand of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: The girl has a fine bundle

parts.note: the pronoun for a girl is she
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A young woman is in possession of a handsome parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle of things tied together, such as corn stalks or papers.

clue.text: Criticise players eating out with no end of fun

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
with no tells us a letter is taken away from the word
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A critic laments that a troupe dining out without any enjoyment deserves a scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating out' reads as dining at a restaurant, but 'eating' is the raw material: 'with no' strips the final letter of 'fun' and 'out' shuffles what remains, EATIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate someone is to rebuke or criticise them severely.

clue.text: Loose grasp of property tenure?

parts.note: loose means at liberty, free
a grasp is a hold

explanation.surface: Asks whether a weak grip on land or buildings is a form of ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Freehold is outright permanent ownership of land or property, a kind of tenure; the question mark flags the playful construction.

clue.text: Married man originally a lady!

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a husband turns out to have been a woman all along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' does not pick a first letter: the original man is Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address or term for a woman of standing.

clue.text: Peevish types no longer available!

definitions.meaning: printing types, or sorts, have run out

explanation.surface: Grumpy, and those characters aren't on sale any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of sorts is an idiom for irritable; read literally, sorts are pieces of type and none remain.

clue.text: Rattle never developed by one in France

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French person who has never been rattled before is shaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unsettle or fluster them, which is what unnerving does.

clue.text: Circles old nurse upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A retired nurse who is distressed goes round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundels are circular discs or emblems, such as the RAF's circle markings.

clue.text: Retainer dispatched to collect regular bits of trivia

indicators.note: one word collects the other, holding it inside

parts.note: something dispatched has been sent

indicators.note: regular bits are every other letter

explanation.surface: An employee is sent out to gather snippets of useless information.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is an old word for a servant, especially one long in a household's employ.

clue.text: Stunned when lorry gets both of us on board

indicators.note: on board means carried inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
the two of us are we
a lorry is a truck

explanation.surface: We are stunned as a lorry takes the pair of us aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means overcome with wonder, stunned.

clue.text: Discovered novel scheme must be exploitation

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its covering, the outside letters, removed

parts.note: a ruse is a crafty scheme

explanation.surface: Finding an innovative plan is said to amount to taking advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found, but means stripped of its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Overuse means using something too much, exploiting it to excess.

clue.text: Pay for person living abroad to accommodate one European

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take in

parts.note: an expat is an expatriate, living outside their own country
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An emigrant is charged for housing a fellow European.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a sin is to atone or make amends for it, to pay for it.

clue.text: Reported facility on net swing

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like this

parts.note: net is trap and facility is ease, so trap followed by ease

explanation.surface: News of a tennis court amenity, perhaps, leading to a swing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a swing bar hung high for acrobats, with a safety net below.

clue.text: Couple however turned up this in the laundry room

parts.note: to couple is to pair or twin

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: but means however

explanation.surface: A pair nonetheless appeared in the utility room.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin tub is an old-style washing machine with separate wash and spin drums.

clue.text: A little tear?

parts.note: looks like a small teardrop, but means a small strip torn from something

explanation.surface: A single small teardrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' sounds like weeping; read it as rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a scrap or strip torn off something, a little piece from tearing.

clue.text: Sticky stuff keeping son in check?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: Is glue the answer to keeping a boy under control?
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky substance exuded by trees.

clue.text: Religious establishment accommodating Italian will get precedence

indicators.note: accommodating means housing the other word inside

parts.note: a priory is a monastery or nunnery headed by a prior

explanation.surface: A monastery taking in an Italian guest will be given precedence.
explanation.definitionFit: Priority is the right to come first, a synonym of precedence.

clue.text: Side order of cream in tea taken occasionally?

indicators.note: taken occasionally means only every other letter is used

explanation.surface: Asks whether cream in one's tea is an occasional treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yoghurt dish served as a side in Indian restaurants.

clue.text: Made an advance fast

definitions.meaning: the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone moved quickly, or loaned money quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent is the past tense of lend, and also the forty-day Christian fast before Easter.

clue.text: Turn, as let off as a consequence

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rental property's tenant arrangement goes wrong as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resultant comes as a consequence of something else; the adjective follows from a cause.

clue.text: Harden against some from Manchester United making a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback here is the letters running back to front
some from means part of the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Fans steel themselves as their football team stages a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure someone is to accustom or toughen them against something unpleasant.

clue.text: Bear has no time to be smooth

indicators.note: has no means the letter is taken out

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it

explanation.surface: An impatient bear lacks the time to be calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To sand wood is to smooth it with sandpaper.

clue.text: Dreary pessimist knew battle is lost

indicators.note: letters that are lost are scattered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy soldier always knew the fight would be lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is an idiom for someone who dampens others' enjoyment with gloom.
